export_host_pattern.title: NFS Export Host Pattern
export_host_pattern.description: The host specification in the NFS export policy, e.g., '*', '0.0.0.0/0', a specific IP, CIDR, or hostname.

export_options.title: NFS Export Options
export_options.description: List of mount options applied to the NFS export entry, e.g., 'rw', 'ro', 'no_root_squash', 'root_squash', 'all_squash', 'sync', 'async'.

root_squash_enabled.title: Root Squash Enabled
root_squash_enabled.description: Indicates whether root_squash is configured on NFS exports, mapping remote root user requests to the anonymous user to prevent privilege escalation.

all_squash_enabled.title: All Squash Enabled
all_squash_enabled.description: Indicates whether all_squash is configured on NFS exports, mapping all remote user requests (including root) to the anonymous user.

transport_encryption_enabled.title: Transport Encryption Enabled
transport_encryption_enabled.description: Whether the NFS or SMB service enforces encryption in transit (e.g., NFSv4 with Kerberos krb5p, SMB encryption, or TLS wrapping). True means encryption is required; false means data is transmitted in cleartext.

smb_signing_required.title: SMB Signing Required
smb_signing_required.description: Whether the SMB server enforces mandatory message signing on all connections, preventing MITM and relay attacks.

smb_signing_enabled.title: SMB Signing Enabled
smb_signing_enabled.description: Whether SMB signing is at least enabled (though not necessarily required). Enabled but not required still allows unsigned connections, leaving relay attacks possible.

protocol_version.title: File Sharing Protocol Version
protocol_version.description: The protocol and version in use for the shared network storage service. Older versions (NFSv2, NFSv3, SMBv1, SMBv2) lack mandatory encryption support.

nfs_auth_flavor.title: NFS Authentication Flavor
nfs_auth_flavor.description: The authentication mechanism configured for NFS exports, determining how client identity is verified (e.g., AUTH_SYS/none, Kerberos krb5, krb5i, krb5p).

kerberos_configured.title: Kerberos Infrastructure Configured for NFS
kerberos_configured.description: Whether a Kerberos KDC and associated keytabs/principals are configured on the NFS server host, enabling cryptographic client authentication.

write_principals.title: Write-Permitted Principals
write_principals.description: List of users, groups, or well-known SIDs granted write (Change or Full Control) access to the SMB share ACL.

full_control_principals.title: Full Control Principals
full_control_principals.description: List of users, groups, or well-known SIDs granted Full Control (read+write+delete+change permissions) on the SMB share.

days_since_last_patch.title: Days Since Last OS/Daemon Patch
days_since_last_patch.description: Number of days elapsed since the last security patch was applied to the OS and storage daemon (nfsd, samba, etc.) on the storage server.

known_unpatched_cves.title: Known Unpatched CVEs for Storage Daemon
known_unpatched_cves.description: List of CVE identifiers that are publicly known to affect the currently installed version of the storage daemon (nfsd, samba, etc.) and have not yet been patched.

storage_daemon_version_eol.title: Storage Daemon Version is End-of-Life
storage_daemon_version_eol.description: Indicates whether the installed version of the storage daemon (nfsd, samba, or equivalent) has reached end-of-life and no longer receives security patches.

storage_ports_allowed_cidr.title: Storage Port Allowed CIDR
storage_ports_allowed_cidr.description: The network CIDR or address range permitted to access storage ports (NFS 2049, mountd 111, SMB 445, iSCSI 3260) in firewall or security group rules.

exposed_storage_protocols.title: Exposed Storage Protocols
exposed_storage_protocols.description: List of storage protocols whose service ports are reachable from non-client network segments. Valid entries: nfs, smb, iscsi, mountd.

client_subnet_restriction_enforced.title: Client Subnet Restriction Enforced
client_subnet_restriction_enforced.description: Whether firewall or security group rules restrict storage port access exclusively to specific, documented client subnets rather than broad or any-source ranges.

mount_event_logging_enabled.title: Mount Event Logging Enabled
mount_event_logging_enabled.description: Whether NFS mount and unmount events are logged to a persistent audit log or syslog facility.

file_access_audit_logging_enabled.title: File Access Audit Logging Enabled
file_access_audit_logging_enabled.description: Whether read, write, and delete operations on NFS-exported paths are captured in an audit log (e.g., via auditd watches, kernel audit rules, or NFSv4 audit support).

failed_auth_logging_enabled.title: Failed Authentication Attempt Logging Enabled
failed_auth_logging_enabled.description: Whether failed authentication and authorization attempts (e.g., denied mounts, AUTH_NULL rejections, Kerberos ticket failures) are logged.

permission_change_logging_enabled.title: Permission Change Logging Enabled
permission_change_logging_enabled.description: Whether changes to export policies, file permissions (chmod/chown), and ACLs on exported paths are captured in an audit log.

volume_encryption_enabled.title: Volume At-Rest Encryption Enabled
volume_encryption_enabled.description: Indicates whether the storage volume has at-rest encryption enabled (e.g., dm-crypt/LUKS, ZFS native encryption, or equivalent).

volume_accessible_over_network.title: Volume Accessible Over Network
volume_accessible_over_network.description: Indicates whether the unencrypted volume is exported or accessible over the network (e.g., via NFS, SMB), compounding the exposure beyond physical access.

export_scope.title: Export Scope
export_scope.description: Indicates whether the NFS export is scoped to specific hosts/networks or is open to all clients (wildcard/global).

export_access_mode.title: Export Access Mode
export_access_mode.description: The read/write permission applied to the export (ro = read-only, rw = read-write).

exports_contain_sensitive_paths.title: Exports Contain Sensitive Paths
exports_contain_sensitive_paths.description: Whether any exported path contains sensitive data such as backup archives, configuration files, credential stores, or home directories.

auth_mechanism.title: Authentication Mechanism
auth_mechanism.description: The authentication flavor used for the NFS export (e.g., sys/AUTH_SYS, krb5, none).

credential_storage_format.title: Credential Storage Format
credential_storage_format.description: How backup agent credentials or service account passwords are stored in configuration files on the storage server.

config_file_world_readable.title: Configuration File World-Readable
config_file_world_readable.description: Whether credential-containing configuration files have permissions that allow read access by non-owner, non-privileged users (e.g., mode 644 or 666).

secrets_manager_enforced.title: Secrets Manager Enforced
secrets_manager_enforced.description: Whether organisational policy or technical controls enforce retrieval of backup credentials from a dedicated secrets manager rather than static configuration files.

snapshot_policy_enabled.title: Read-Only Snapshot Policy Enabled
snapshot_policy_enabled.description: Indicates whether periodic read-only snapshots are configured and enabled for the shared storage volume, protecting against overwrite or deletion of backup data.

worm_policy_enabled.title: WORM Policy Enabled
worm_policy_enabled.description: Indicates whether a WORM or immutable storage policy is enforced on the share, preventing modification or deletion of stored data within the retention period.

snapshot_retention_days.title: Snapshot Retention Period (Days)
snapshot_retention_days.description: The number of days snapshots are retained before being automatically purged. A value of zero or very low values provide insufficient protection against ransomware or insider threat scenarios.

daemon_process_user.title: Daemon Process User Account
daemon_process_user.description: The OS user account under which the NFS or SMB daemon process runs (e.g., root, nfsnobody, daemon, smbuser).

dedicated_service_account_exists.title: Dedicated Low-Privilege Service Account Exists
dedicated_service_account_exists.description: Whether a dedicated non-root, non-login service account has been created and configured for the NFS/SMB daemon.

daemon_has_cap_net_bind_or_sys_admin.title: Daemon Has Elevated Linux Capabilities
daemon_has_cap_net_bind_or_sys_admin.description: Whether the daemon process has been granted elevated Linux capabilities (CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, or similar) beyond what is required.

uses_default_vendor_credentials.title: Uses Default Vendor Credentials
uses_default_vendor_credentials.description: Indicates whether the storage management interface or backup agent is still using default credentials provided by the vendor.

service_account_shared_across_systems.title: Service Account Shared Across Multiple Systems
service_account_shared_across_systems.description: Indicates whether a single service account credential set is reused across multiple storage or backup systems, creating a single point of compromise.

credential_rotation_enforced.title: Credential Rotation Policy Enforced
credential_rotation_enforced.description: Indicates whether a credential rotation policy is enforced for storage management and backup service accounts, ensuring credentials are periodically changed.

disk_quotas_enabled.title: Disk Quotas Enabled
disk_quotas_enabled.description: Whether per-user or per-share disk quotas are configured and enforced on the NFS/shared storage volume.

quota_scope.title: Quota Scope
quota_scope.description: The granularity at which quotas are applied: per-user, per-group, per-share, or none.

enabled_storage_protocols.title: Enabled Storage Protocols
enabled_storage_protocols.description: List of storage and management protocols currently enabled on the storage server (e.g., nfs, smb, ftp, telnet, rsh, http, https, ssh).

insecure_legacy_protocols_justified.title: Insecure Legacy Protocols Have Documented Business Justification
insecure_legacy_protocols_justified.description: Whether any enabled insecure/legacy protocols (FTP, telnet, rsh, HTTP management) have formal documented justification and compensating controls on record.
